questions.question: Which of the following is a Government scheme that aims mainly to skill rural youth who are poor and provide them with jobs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)** is a flagship program launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) under the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM).
 
• The scheme focuses on **providing skill development training** to rural poor youth and ensuring their placement in formal employment sectors.
 
• It specifically targets individuals aged **15 to 35 years** from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, with an emphasis on women, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and minority communities.
 
• The program operates on a public-private partnership model and provides free skill training in various industries, including retail, hospitality, healthcare, construction, and automotive sectors.
 
• DDU-GKY has an **ambitious agenda** to train 28 lakh rural youth and place at least 70% of them in sustainable jobs by 2022.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**:

 
 
• Launched on August 28, 2014, by PM Narendra Modi, PMJDY is a national financial inclusion program aimed at expanding affordable access to financial services such as bank accounts, remittances, credit, insurance, and pensions.
 
• The scheme enables every household to have at least one basic savings bank deposit account.
 
• Beneficiaries receive **accidental insurance coverage of Rs. 2 lakh** and a life insurance cover of Rs. 30,000 for eligible beneficiaries.
 
• Under this scheme, overdraft facilities of up to Rs. 10,000 are provided to account holders after six months of satisfactory operation.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**:
 
 
• Launched on May 9, 2015, PMSBY is an accident insurance scheme providing affordable insurance coverage for accidental death and disability.
 
• Individuals aged 18 to 70 years can avail of the scheme by paying a nominal premium of Rs. 20 annually.
 
• The scheme offers a risk coverage of Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability.
 
 
 
• **UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All)**:
 
 
• UJALA was launched in 2015 to promote energy efficiency by distributing LED bulbs at subsidized rates to households across India.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce electricity bills, decrease energy consumption, and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• It is implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.

questions.question: Which corridor enhances India's access to Central Asia through Chabahar Port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-South Transport Corridor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **North-South Transport Corridor (NSTC)** is a multimodal transportation network aimed at enhancing connectivity between India, Russia, Iran, and Central Asia.
 
• The corridor includes the use of **Chabahar Port** in Iran, which serves as a crucial gateway for India to access Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
 
• It was officially established in **2000** by India, Iran, and Russia and has since expanded to include several other countries.
 
• The NSTC reduces transportation time and costs for goods traveling between India and Central Asia, Europe, and Russia via a combination of sea, rail, and road networks.
 
• The strategic use of Chabahar Port is part of India's broader geopolitical and economic strategy to counter China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and strengthen India's trade and energy ties with Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **East-West Corridor**

 
 
• The East-West Corridor is a part of India’s **Golden Quadrilateral project** aimed at improving road connectivity across the country.
 
• This corridor connects Silchar in Assam (Eastern India) to Porbandar in Gujarat (Western India).
 
• It primarily focuses on domestic connectivity and has no direct role in enhancing India’s access to Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **India-Myanmar Highway**
 
 
• The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway is an important infrastructure project aimed at improving connectivity between India and Southeast Asia.
 
• This highway connects Moreh in Manipur (India) to Mae Sot in Thailand via Myanmar.
 
• While significant for India's Act East Policy, it does not facilitate access to Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **South Asian Maritime Path**
 
 
• This term generally refers to maritime routes used for trade within South Asia and beyond, including the Indian Ocean Region.
 
• It is not a formal or specific corridor and does not pertain to Central Asian connectivity through Chabahar Port.

• The Peninsular Plateau

 
 
• ​Geologically, the physiographic division of India that is supposed to be one of the most stable land blocks is the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• A tableland made up of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks are known as the Peninsular plateau.
 
• It belongs to the oldest landmass because it was created by the fracturing and drifting of the Gondwana region.

• The peninsular plateau's climate and black soil make it an ideal place for the cultivation of cotton. Since ancient times, cotton has been essential to the trade and economic growth of India.

questions.question: When was Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) passed by parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1999**__.

__
 
• **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)**__

 
 
• It is a set of regulations that empowers the Reserve Bank of India to pass regulations and enables the Government of India to pass rules relating to foreign exchange with respect to the foreign trade policy of India.
 
• The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) was introduced by the Indian Government in 1999, replacing the previous Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) of 1973.
 
• It was passed on** 29 December 1999.**
 
• FEMA became an act on the 1st day of June 2000.

__
 
• Wildlife Sanctuaries are designated areas that provide protection to both flora and fauna while allowing regulated human activities such as grazing, tourism, and resource collection.
 
• These sanctuaries aim to conserve biodiversity by protecting endangered species and maintaining ecosystems.
 
• Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, which defines rules for wildlife conservation in India.
 
• Unlike National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries have less stringent restrictions on human activities, making them suitable for coexistence between local communities and wildlife conservation efforts.
 
• Examples include Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary in Rajasthan and Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala.

• National Parks are strictly protected areas established for the conservation of wildlife and natural habitats.

• Limited tourism and research activities may be permitted under strict regulations.
 
• Examples include Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand and Kaziranga National Park in Assam.
 
• Since National Parks do not generally allow human activities (except regulated tourism), Statement 1 is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Difference between National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries**
 
 
• National Parks have stricter rules and provide complete protection to wildlife, while Wildlife Sanctuaries allow limited human activities.
 
• National Parks are notified by the central government, whereas Wildlife Sanctuaries can be notified by state governments as well.
 
• The legal framework for both is provided by the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Biodiversity Conservation**
 
 
• Biodiversity conservation ensures ecological balance, genetic diversity, and the survival of species.
 
• Protected areas such as National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries play a crucial role in conserving biodiversity.

questions.question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vitamin D**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a condition that affects bone development in children. It causes the bones to become soft and weak, which can lead to bone deformities.
 
• The primary cause of rickets is a **deficiency of vitamin D**.
 
• Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the diet, which are critical for healthy bone formation.
 
• Without sufficient vitamin D, the body cannot properly regulate calcium and phosphate levels, leading to the symptoms of rickets.
 
• Common sources of vitamin D include exposure to sunlight, which triggers vitamin D production in the skin, and dietary sources such as fatty fish, liver, and fortified foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rickets can also be caused by genetic factors, certain medical conditions, or malabsorption disorders that affect the body's ability to process vitamin D.
 
• Preventing rickets involves ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D through diet and supplementation, as well as sensible sun exposure.
 
• Treatment for rickets typically includes vitamin D and calcium supplements, and in severe cases, corrective surgery may be required to address bone deformities.
 
• Public health measures, such as fortifying foods with vitamin D, have been effective in reducing the incidence of rickets in many parts of the world.

• Convinced to stand up for the safety of the Kashmiri Pandits by his uncle, Gobind Rai, who later became Guru Gobind Singh, Guru Tegh Bahadur travelled to Delhi.
